headline: DayOne, a Singapore data centre operator, is pushing ahead with its US share sale while two other data centre firms, AirTrunk and Firmus, have reportedly delayed or withdrawn theirs.
score_reason: Multi-billion-dollar AI infrastructure listing going ahead against a weak market, corroborated by the Business Times; the TikTok link in The Information's headline could not be checked.
importance_line: It tests whether investors will still fund a fast-growing but loss-making builder of AI data centres while peers retreat, which matters to the investors and customers of such firms, but the final price is unknown and the nature of the TikTok link is not known.
summary: The Information reports that DayOne, a Singapore data centre operator, is pushing ahead with a share sale that its headline describes as "tied to TikTok". The Business Times reports that DayOne filed in October for a US Nasdaq listing to raise as much as $5 billion at a potential valuation of about $20 billion, after its revenue more than tripled to $512 million in the first half of 2026, while AirTrunk is said to be delaying its listing and Firmus withdrew its own.
notes: The Information article not readable (paywall); only its headline is used. The second sentence is from the Business Times (15 Oct 2026 and 6 Oct 2026), read in full: https://www.businesstimes.com.sg/companies-markets/why-tech-data-centre-ipos-are-facing-delays-and-what-investors-can-expect-market-now . What 'tied to TikTok' means was not found.
